This assembly process is derived from [Immcantation Documentation: Illumina MiSeq 2x250 BCR mRNA](https://presto.readthedocs.io/en/stable/workflows/Greiff2014_Workflow.html)

Schematically:

<center>
![](/Users/emoseley/Desktop/Pipeline.png){width=50%}
</center>

### (1) Paired-End Assembly (a bit).

```{bash, eval = F}
docker run -v /Users/emoseley/VHH/data:/data  immcantation/suite:4.4.0  \
  AssemblePairs.py align -1 /data/1_3_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq -2 /data/1_3_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq \
  --coord illumina --rc tail --maxerror 0.1 \
  --outname S1
```



## (4) Deduplication and Filtering

The last stage of the workflow involves two filtering steps to yield the final repertoire. First, the set of unique sequences is identified using the `CollapseSeq.py `tool, allowing for up to 20 interior N-valued positions (`-n 20` and `--inner`), and **you requiring that all reads considered duplicates share the same C-region primer annotation (`--uf CPRIMER`)**. Additionally, the V-segment primer annotations of the set of duplicate reads are propagated into the annotation of each retained unique sequence (`--cf VPRIMER` and `--act set`):

```{bash, eval = F}
docker run -v /Users/emoseley/VHH/data:/data immcantation/suite:4.4.0  \
CollapseSeq.py -s /data/S1-REV_primers-pass.fastq -n 20 --inner --uf CPRIMER \
    --cf VPRIMER --act set --outname S1
```

```
docker run -v /Users/emoseley/VHH/data:/data immcantation/suite:4.4.0  \
CollapseSeq.py -s /data/S1-REV_primers-pass.fastq -n 20 --inner --uf CPRIMER \
    --cf VPRIMER --act set --outname S1
    
       START> CollapseSeq
        FILE> S1-REV_primers-pass.fastq
 MAX_MISSING> 20
 UNIQ_FIELDS> CPRIMER
 COPY_FIELDS> VPRIMER
COPY_ACTIONS> set
   MAX_FIELD> None
   MIN_FIELD> None
       INNER> True
KEEP_MISSING> False

PROGRESS> [0 missing] 16:51:47 |####################| 100% (157,364) 0.1 min

      OUTPUT> S1_collapse-unique.fastq
   SEQUENCES> 157364
      UNIQUE> 123826
   DUPLICATE> 33538
UNDETERMINED> 0
         END> CollapseSeq

```

`CollapseSeq` stores the count of duplicate reads for each sequence in the `DUPCOUNT` annotation. Following duplicate removal, the data is subset to only those unique sequence with at least two representative reads by using the group subcommand of `SplitSeq.py` on the count field (`-f DUPCOUNT`) and specifying a numeric threshold (`--num 2`):

```{bash, eval = F}
docker run -v /Users/emoseley/VHH/data:/data immcantation/suite:4.4.0  \
  SplitSeq.py group -s /data/S1_collapse-unique.fastq -f DUPCOUNT --num 2 --outname S1
```

```
docker run -v /Users/emoseley/VHH/data:/data immcantation/suite:4.4.0  \
  SplitSeq.py group -s /data/S1_collapse-unique.fastq -f DUPCOUNT --num 2 --outname S1
    START> SplitSeq
  COMMAND> group
     FILE> S1_collapse-unique.fastq
    FIELD> DUPCOUNT
THRESHOLD> 2.0

PROGRESS> 16:54:11 |####################| 100% (123,826) 0.6 min

  OUTPUT1> S1_under-2.fastq
  OUTPUT2> S1_atleast-2.fastq
SEQUENCES> 123826
    PARTS> 2
      END> SplitSeq
```


## (5) Creating an annotation table

Finally, the annotations, including duplicate read count (`DUPCOUNT`), isotype (`CPRIMER`) and V-segment primer (`VPRIMER`), of the final repertoire are then extracted from the `SplitSeq.py` output into a tab-delimited file using the table subcommand of `ParseHeaders.py`:

```{bash, eval = F}
docker run -v /Users/emoseley/VHH/data:/data immcantation/suite:4.4.0  \
  ParseHeaders.py table -s /data/S1_atleast-2.fastq -f ID DUPCOUNT CPRIMER VPRIMER
```

```
docker run -v /Users/emoseley/VHH/data:/data immcantation/suite:4.4.0  \
  ParseHeaders.py table -s /data/S1_atleast-2.fastq -f ID DUPCOUNT CPRIMER VPRIMER
  START> ParseHeaders
COMMAND> table
   FILE> S1_atleast-2.fastq

PROGRESS> 16:55:31 |####################| 100% (7,747) 0.0 min

   OUTPUT> S1_atleast-2_headers.tab
SEQUENCES> 7747
     PASS> 7747
     FAIL> 0
      END> ParseHeaders
```

#### Check log

```{r}
tmp <- read.csv("~/VHH/data/S1_atleast-2_headers.tab", sep = '\t', header = T, stringsAsFactors = F)

# CPrimer is unmasked
table(tmp$CPRIMER)
# VPrimer is masked
table(tmp$VPRIMER)
```

### Prep for IMGT

```
# Copy over the file
cp S1_atleast-2.fastq ~/ncbi-igblast-1.17.1/
# Change the directory
cd ~/ncbi-igblast-1.17.1
```
## Convert the file to fasta

```{r, echo = T, eval = F}
# Arguments
args <- c("S1_atleast-2.fastq")
# args = commandArgs(trailingOnly=TRUE)

# Directory
directory <- "/Users/emoseley/VHH/data/"

# Set current working directory to ncbi-igblast-1.17.1
setwd("~/ncbi-igblast-1.17.1")

file_origin <- paste("~/ncbi-igblast-1.17.1/", args[1], sep = '')
file_output <- gsub(".fastq", ".fasta", file_origin)
results <- gsub(".fastq", '.fmt7', args)
```

### IMGT

```{bash, eval = F}
bin/igblastn -germline_db_V database/alpaca_vhh_clean/alpaca_V -germline_db_D database/alpaca_vhh_clean/alpaca_D -germline_db_J database/alpaca_vhh_clean/alpaca_J -domain_system imgt -ig_seqtype Ig -organism alpaca -auxiliary_data optional_file/alpaca_gl.aux -outfmt '7 std qseq sseq btop' -query ~/ncbi-igblast-1.17.1/S1_atleast-2.fasta -out ~/ncbi-igblast-1.17.1/S1_atleast-2.fmt7
```

```
# Copy back to data
cp S1_atleast-2.fmt7 ~/VHH/data
cp S1_atleast-2.fasta ~/VHH/data
```

### Make Database

```{bash, eval = F}
docker run -v /Users/emoseley/VHH/data:/data immcantation/suite:4.4.0 \
  MakeDb.py igblast -i /data/S1_atleast-2.fmt7 -s /data/S1_atleast-2.fasta \
  -r /data/imgt-data/imgt_gapped_alpaca_IGHV.fasta \
  /data/imgt-data/imgt_gapped_alpaca_IGHD.fasta  \
  /data/imgt-data/imgt_gapped_alpaca_IGHJ.fasta \
  --outdir /data/ --failed --format airr --extended
```
